summary: This bill requires the Secretary of State to designate 30 listed Iran-backed militias and groups (including Ansarallah/Houthis and several Iraqi Popular Mobilization Units) as foreign terrorist organizations within 90 days and requires the President to decide within 60 days whether to impose terrorism sanctions on many of them, with follow-up reporting.

scores.thoughts: The bill focuses exclusively on designating foreign terrorist organizations and imposing sanctions. It contains no provisions that authorize, expand, or reduce any form of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or tax policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy or systems.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.

The bill designates organizations as foreign terrorist organizations pursuant to section 219(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act. While FTO designations carry immigration consequences (such as inadmissibility), the bill's primary purpose is terrorism sanctions rather than immigration policy reform, making any connection tangential at best.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive rights.
The bill contains no provisions that alter military or defense spending levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs or social safety net policies.
The bill contains no provisions related to education policy or funding.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill addresses foreign terrorist designations and sanctions rather than domestic criminal justice reforms such as sentencing or policing.
While sanctions can indirectly affect transactions, the bill does not engage with broader trade policy, tariffs, or globalization frameworks.
The bill contains no provisions addressing deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill contains no provisions that expand, maintain, or reduce foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill contains no provisions related to labor rights or unions.
The bill contains no provisions addressing religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
